name: Aloo Tuk
subtitle: twice-fried smashed potatoes, crisp outside and floury within, dusted with amchur

ingredients.qty: 600g small potatoes, peeled and halved (or large ones in 3cm chunks)

ingredients.note: check the blend if you need this strictly gluten-free, as some brands carry compounded hing

prepNotes: Peel and halve the potatoes and keep them in cold water until you fry, then drain and dry them completely on a cloth — wet potatoes spit violently in hot oil.
Tuk is fried twice with a cooling gap in between. Budget 10 minutes of rest between the two fries; skipping it gives you soft, oily potatoes.
Mix the amchur, chaat masala, chilli powder, black salt, pepper and salt in a small bowl before you start frying.

steps.text: Heat the oil to medium — a potato piece dropped in should bubble steadily around the edges, not fizz furiously.
Fry the potatoes in two batches for 8-10 minutes each, until pale gold and a skewer slides in easily. They should be cooked through but not coloured much.
steps.tip: Too hot here and the outside seals before the inside softens, which is the classic tuk failure.

steps.text: Lift them out onto a rack and let them cool for 10 minutes.
Flatten each piece with the heel of your hand or the flat of a knife to about 1.5cm, so the edges crack open.
steps.tip: Press firmly but stop before it falls apart — those cracked edges are where the crispness comes from.

steps.text: Raise the oil to high, until a scrap of potato surfaces immediately.
Fry the flattened pieces again in batches, 3-4 minutes, until deep golden and audibly crisp when knocked against the ladle.
Drain on a rack rather than paper so the undersides do not steam soft.
While still very hot, toss with the spice mix and taste for salt.
steps.tip: Season them hot. Once they cool, the powder sits on top instead of sticking.

steps.text: Serve at once, alongside sindhi kadhi and rice as tradition has it, or on their own with tea.

storage: Best within the hour. Fried, unflattened potatoes hold 4 hours at room temperature and can be smashed and given their second fry just before eating; leftovers go soft and reheat poorly.
